key_insight: CM2 uses checklist-style rewards that break open-ended, multi-turn, multi-step tasks into verifiable subgoals, enabling reinforcement learning to train agentic tool-using policies without needing exhaustive executable tool environments.
problem_solved: Addresses the difficulty of applying RL to real-world assistant workflows where objectives are open-ended and lack verifiable rewards, multi-turn/multi-step agentic tool use is underexplored, and building/maintaining full executable tool environments is expensive and unscalable.
method: Introduce checklist rewards: decompose tasks into verifiable subgoals that provide intermediate reward signals across turns and steps.
Train RL policies to plan and invoke external tools across multi-turn interactions, optimizing checklist completion rather than only final outcomes.
Reduce reliance on costly executable environments by leveraging verifier-based rewards, synthetic or offline interactions, and checklist-driven supervision to scale training.
impact: Makes RL practical and scalable for building multi-turn, tool-using agents by improving learning signal quality, interpretability, and sample efficiency while lowering environment engineering costs—enabling deployment in real-world assistant workflows.

paper_title: CM2: Reinforcement Learning with Checklist Rewards for Multi-Turn and Multi-Step Agentic Tool Use
paper_authors: Zhen Zhang, Kaiqiang Song, Xun Wang, Yebowen Hu, Weixiang Yan
